Large total tumor volume (98 mL) and deep white‑matter and ependymal invasion further favor a high‑grade IDH‑wildtype lesion. Cortical involvement could suggest IDH‑mutant disease, but the preponderance of high‑grade features outweighs this. Thus the evidence points to IDH‑wildtype.

While frontal‑cortical location can be seen in oligodendroglioma, the aggressive radiologic profile (thick enhancing rim, necrosis, ependymal invasion) aligns better with a 1p/19q non‑codeleted, IDH‑wildtype glioblastoma.
